perspective:
From Sara Manuelito’s perspective, she has access to the following:

- She knows Shirley Whiteplume as a long-time colleague and close friend; they have worked together at a community health center for several years, and she knows Shirley is a nurse.
- She attended the funeral of a mutual patient with Shirley.
- At the funeral, she observed Shirley’s somber demeanor and suspected Shirley was deeply affected by the loss.
- She heard Shirley say it had been tough and that she kept thinking about whether something more could have been done. Sara responded that they did everything they could and should remember the good care and moments of joy they provided. Shirley said it was hard to let go.
- During a coffee break at work, Sara raised the patient’s treatment decisions because she sensed Shirley felt burdened. She heard Shirley say she felt responsible and wondered if pushing for a different approach might have helped. Sara said they made the best decisions with the information they had and that Shirley should not carry the burden alone. Shirley said she appreciated it but found it hard to accept.
- In their office, Sara observed Shirley being reserved and minimally expressive. Sara told her it was okay to be open about her feelings. Shirley said she was not sure she could and did not want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara said showing emotion does not make her weak and it is healthy to express feelings among friends. Shirley said maybe Sara was right and she would try to be more open.
- Sara later felt her previous confrontation may have been too harsh, so she apologized. Shirley said it had been a bit much but she knew Sara meant well and appreciated the apology. Sara said she was there for Shirley in whatever way needed. Shirley thanked her and said they should keep talking because it helps.
- Later, Sara noticed Shirley seemed to be doing better. She asked how Shirley was feeling. Shirley said she felt better thanks to their talks and Sara’s support. Sara suggested spending more time together outside work. Shirley agreed and suggested planning something for the weekend.
